title: Region-bound evidence broker: API contract, delivery guarantees, and retention orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a region-aware evidence broker service that provides a stable API and webhook contracts for audit/retention/residency events. The broker must: 1) accept evidence ingestion with explicit residency declarations, 2) emit verified delivery events to customer webhooks with idempotency and signing, 3) enforce retention TTL and auto-evict/archival workflows, and 4) surface an HTTP API for downstream consumers to query evidence location and retention state. This ticket covers API contract, SLA guarantees, signing format, and orchestration handoffs to archival and ledger services.
acceptance_criteria: API spec published and approved with residency header and enforcement semantics
Webhook delivery contract documented with idempotency keys, signature scheme, and retry semantics
End-to-end test demonstrating ingestion in eu-west region and delivery to an EU-resident webhook endpoint with signed payload and correct residency assertion
Retention enforcement triggers archival workflow at TTL expiry and creates a signed deletion record in the audit ledger
Metrics and dashboards for webhook success rate, delivery latency, and residency mismatches added to Console observability
Security review completed and threat-model mitigations captured
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight evidence-broker service that sits between upstream ingestion (runtime/ingest API) and downstream delivery/archival subsystems. The broker will persist minimal metadata (evidence id, residency tag, TTL, delivery status, signed receipts) in the region-local ledger. Delivery will use a webhook worker with exactly-once semantics via idempotency keys and signature verification. Retention lifecycle will trigger a serverless archival or deletion job depending on residency rules. The broker exposes a REST API and emits event traces to the existing compliance event bus for audit and observability.
architecture_notes:
- Use region-local ledger (existing residency-ledger) for authoritative location and TTL to avoid cross-region reads.
- Webhook signer: ED25519 key per-region stored in KMS; signatures include evidence_id, residency, ttl_expiry, and broker_nonce.
- Delivery guarantees: persistent queue with exponential backoff and dead-letter to a 'manual review' queue for EU-resident webhooks when delivery fails repeatedly.
- Avoid shipping full evidence payloads across regions; deliver pointers + signed residency assertion to comply with data sovereignty.
implementation_plan: Draft OpenAPI spec for broker ingestion and status endpoints
Implement minimal broker service with region-local ledger integration
Add webhook worker with idempotency and signature header (X-Evidence-Signature)
Integrate retention TTL worker to trigger archival/deletion flows
Add unit/integration tests and an E2E test harness that exercises residency assertions
Run security review and fix findings, then document runbook for failed deliveries
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger writes and TTL calculation, integration tests for webhook delivery and signature verification, chaos test to simulate regional failover with fallback to cross-region metadata-only deliveries, and a compliance test that verifies data never leaves declared residency when policy requires.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary in eu-west with synthetic customers and 2% of ingestion traffic; 2) Observe delivery metrics and manual review queue growth for 48h; 3) Gradual ramp to 25%, then 100% after SLA and telemetry checks; 4) Enable archival/deletion automation for non-customer-critical evidence after two successful weeks on canary.
